bibliographic.title: Ethical and Legal Governance of Generative AI in Chinese Healthcare
bibliographic.citation_apa: Jia, J., & Zhao, S. (2025). Ethical and Legal Governance of Generative AI in Chinese Healthcare. Journal of Multidisciplinary Healthcare. https://doi.org/10.2147/JMDH.S541271

methodology.method_family: legal and ethical policy analysis with literature review
methodology.study_design: perspective article reviewing legal/regulatory frameworks and academic literature; proposes governance framework
methodology.technology_context: generative artificial intelligence, ChatGPT, GPT-3, Deepseek, large-scale language modeling, conversational chatbots in medical applications

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article directly addresses ethical and legal governance of generative AI in Chinese healthcare, reviews regulatory frameworks and literature, and proposes a governance framework. It aligns with regulated-domain generative AI governance but, in the provided text, emphasizes policy and legal-ethical analysis rather than operational conversational governance mechanisms such as guardrails, observability, or human oversight workflows.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and partial page 2 are available; full methods, literature selection criteria, and conversational AI governance depth cannot be verified.

appraisal.notes: Provided excerpt states legal-ethical review and framework development but does not describe systematic search, inclusion criteria, or detailed analytical protocol. Findings are clearly summarized in the abstract; limitations section not visible in excerpt.

cerqual.explanation: The study presents a coherent legal-ethical governance focus for generative AI in healthcare and clear high-level findings, but methodological transparency is limited in the available text and the contribution appears primarily framework-oriented rather than empirically or operationally grounded.

coding.theme: Ethical and legal governance of generative AI in regulated healthcare
coding.subtheme: Chinese healthcare regulatory and ethical framework gaps

synthesis.main_claim: China is actively constructing an ethical and legal governance framework for generative AI in healthcare, but the regulatory system remains inadequate and faces challenges including lagging rules, unclear AI legal status, immature medical AI training data standards, and weak inter-agency coordination; the authors propose a legal-ethical governance framework and broader measures such as algorithm transparency, standardized medical data management, AI legislation, and a global AI ethics review committee.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a legal-ethical governance framework for generative AI in the Chinese medical field and synthesizes regulatory and academic perspectives on key risks and policy gaps.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence on legal-ethical governance frameworks, regulatory challenges, and proposed policy responses for generative AI in regulated healthcare; useful contextual material for China-specific healthcare governance rather than primary evidence on conversational system operational controls.

evidence.excerpt: Ethical and Legal Governance of Generative AI in Chinese Healthcare Jinrun Jia, Shiqiao Zhao

evidence.claim: Peer review status not stated in provided text
Study reviews legal/regulatory frameworks and literature
evidence.excerpt: This study reviews and analyzes the legal and regulatory frameworks established in China for the application of generative AI in healthcare, as well as relevant academic literature.

evidence.claim: Regulatory system remains inadequate with specific challenges
evidence.excerpt: the regulatory system remains inadequate and faces numerous challenges. These challenges include lagging regulatory rules; an unclear legal status of AI in laws such as the Civil Code; immature standards and regulatory schemes for medical AI training data; and the lack of a coordinated regulatory mechanism among different government departments.
this study attempts to establish a governance framework for generative AI in the medical field in China from both legal and ethical perspectives

evidence.claim: Key risk areas include human agency, fairness, and liability
evidence.excerpt: These risks are manifested in three key areas: first, the potential erosion of human agency; second, issues of fairness and justice; and third, questions of liability and responsibility.

evidence.claim: Generative AI risks include accuracy, transparency, privacy, ethics, and bias
evidence.excerpt: However, risks persist in terms of accuracy, transparency, data privacy, ethics, and bias.

evidence.claim: Conversational chatbots appear in medical generative AI context
evidence.excerpt: Conversational chatbots take on some of the duties of medical professionals.

evidence.claim: GPT-3 used in medical applications during COVID-19
evidence.excerpt: AI models capable of generative tasks, such as GPT-3, were widely utilized for various medical applications.

evidence.claim: Study focuses on legal and ethical analysis with some clinical/technical coverage
evidence.excerpt: This study primarily focuses on legal and ethical analysis, while also covering specific analyses of clinical and technical impacts.

evidence.claim: Proposed policy responses include transparency, data management, and legislation
evidence.excerpt: This includes enhancing algorithm transparency, standardizing medical data management, and promoting AI legislation.

evidence.claim: Proposal for global ethics review mechanism
evidence.excerpt: efforts should be made to establish a global AI ethics review committee to promote the formation of internationally unified ethical and legal review mechanisms.
